### Building a New PC – Step‑by‑Step Guide Below is a practical, beginner‑friendly walkthrough. Feel free to skip sections you already know or dive deeper into the parts that interest you. | # | What to Do | Why It Matters | Tips | |---|------------|----------------|------| | 1 | **Plan & Budget** | Decide what you’ll use it for (gaming, video editing, office work) and set a budget. | Use online PC builders (PCPartPicker, BuildMyPC) to estimate costs and check compatibility. | | 2 | **Choose Components** | Pick CPU, motherboard, RAM, GPU, storage, PSU, case, cooling, OS. | • **CPU + Motherboard**: Match socket (e.g., Intel LGA 1200, AMD AM4).
• **RAM**: DDR4/DDR5, speed matters for gaming/CPU‑heavy tasks.
• **GPU**: Depends on resolution & refresh rate.
• **Storage**: SSD for OS + games, HDD for bulk.
• **PSU**: 80+ Gold, 500–750 W for mid‑range builds.
• **Case**: ATX, Micro‑ATX, Mini‑ITX; ensure airflow. | | 3 | **Gather Tools & Workspace** | Screwdrivers (Phillips), anti‑static wrist strap, cable ties, thermal paste (if not pre‑applied). | Work on a clean, flat surface; keep components away from static surfaces. | | 4 | **Prepare the Case** | Remove side panels, install standoffs for motherboard, mount PSU. | Label standoffs to match motherboard layout. | | 5 | **Install the CPU** | Open CPU socket, align pin‑to‑pin, secure latch. | Don’t touch pins; use the notch as a guide. | | 6 | **Apply Thermal Paste & Install Cooler** | If cooler doesn’t have paste pre‑applied, apply a pea‑size amount. Attach cooler, connect fan header. | For air coolers, use the mounting bracket; for liquid coolers, attach radiator to case. | | 7 | **Insert RAM** | Open DIMM slots, align notch, press firmly until latches click. | Install in pairs for dual‑channel mode. | | 8 | **Mount Motherboard** | Align with standoffs and I/O shield, screw down. | Double‑check all screws; don’t overtighten. | | 9 | **Install Storage** | Mount SSD/HDD in drive bays or M.2 slot. Connect SATA data & power cables if using SATA drives. | Label cables for easier troubleshooting. | | 10 | **Install GPU** | Insert into PCI‑Express x16 slot, secure with screws, connect power cables. | Ensure the slot is fully seated; use a small screwdriver to lock the slot latch. | | 11 | **Connect Power Supply** | Attach 24‑pin ATX, 8‑pin EPS, PCI‑e power to GPU, SATA power to drives. | Keep cables tidy; use cable ties. | | 12 | **Cable Management** | Route cables behind motherboard tray, use Velcro straps. | Good airflow reduces heat; avoid blocking fans. | | 13 | **Final Checks** | Verify all connections, no loose screws, no stray wires. | Double‑check that the PSU switch is off before powering on. | | 14 | **Power On & BIOS Setup** | Turn on PSU, press power button. Enter BIOS (usually F2, DEL). | Set boot order: USB/DVD first for OS installation. | | 15 | **Install Operating System** | Boot from USB/DVD, follow installer prompts. | Install drivers after OS is up: chipset, GPU, audio. | | 16 | **Update & Test** | Run Windows Update, install latest GPU drivers. Run stress tests (Prime95, FurMark) to confirm stability. | Monitor temperatures; keep them below 80 °C under load. | --- #### Quick Component Checklist | Category | Example Choices (Mid‑Range) | Notes | |----------|-----------------------------|-------| | CPU | Intel Core i5‑13600K / AMD Ryzen 5 7600X | Good for gaming & multitasking | | Motherboard | MSI MPG B660 Gaming Plus / ASUS TUF Gaming B650-PLUS | Supports chosen CPU, has good VRM | | RAM | Corsair Vengeance LPX 16 GB (2×8 GB) DDR4‑3200 | Dual‑channel, 16 GB is sweet spot | | GPU | NVIDIA RTX 3060 Ti / AMD Radeon RX 6700 XT | 1440p gaming | | Storage | Samsung 970 EVO Plus 1 TB NVMe SSD | Fast boot & load times | | PSU | EVGA 600 W1, 80+ WHITE 600W | 80+ Gold is better for efficiency | | Case | NZXT H510 | Compact, good airflow | | Cooling | Cooler Master Hyper 212 RGB | Air cooler, easy to install | | OS | Windows 11 Home | Or Linux if you prefer open source | --- #### Common Pitfalls & How to Avoid Them | Issue | Fix | |-------|-----| | **Short circuits** | Use anti‑static wrist strap; keep metal contacts away from each other. | | **Overheating** | Ensure proper airflow, use quality thermal paste, keep dust out. | | **Component incompatibility** | Verify socket, chipset, RAM type, PSU wattage before buying. | | **Boot failure** | Check BIOS boot order, reseat GPU, ensure PSU is connected. | | **Driver conflicts** | Install chipset drivers first, then GPU drivers. | --- #### Resources - **PCPartPicker** – Build planner & price comparison. - **YouTube Channels** – Linus Tech Tips, JayzTwoCents, Paul's Hardware. - **Reddit** – r/buildapc for community help. - **Manufacturer Manuals** – Always read the motherboard, PSU, and case manuals. --- ### Final Thought Building a PC is a rewarding project that gives you control over performance, aesthetics, and future upgrades. Take your time, double‑check every connection, and enjoy the process! If you hit a snag, feel free to ask for more detailed help on any step. Happy building!
